pages.content:
Docs
/
Overview
Documentation

Create component documentation in Figma, copy specs for your coding agent, or pull a published library’s specs and tokens into your repository.

Start with your workflow
Document a design system
Create component specs and foundation references inside Figma.
Give an agent design context
Copy component specs, variables, or styles without creating canvas docs first.
Connect a repository
Publish a library and pull its specs and tokens with the CLI.

Canvas documentation and Copy for AI are free. The person publishing a library needs Pro. Developers pulling it need a library ID and pull key.

Find a specific answer
Output formats

What each export contains, where files land, and which format to use.

CLI commands

Every command, supported flags, selection rules, and exit codes.

Configuration

Project settings, pull keys, token options, and automation.

Schemas

Download schemas, validate canonical exports, and understand source IDs.

Three terms to know
Canvas docs
Readable Figma documentation connected to its source. The Library helps you check and update it.
Context
Structured component specifications and design tokens. Component copies use YAML; foundation copies use the Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) JSON format.
Published library
A snapshot uploaded from Figma. The CLI downloads this snapshot, so unpublished design changes do not appear in a pull.
Versions covered here

This reference covers CLI 0.4.0 and canonical Context schema 5.1.0. The v5 schema URL identifies the major contract; the artifact contains its exact schema version.

The CLI delivers design context for your developers or coding agent to use during implementation. Optional AI writing helps draft documentation in the plugin.

For changes over time, read the changelog. To help improve Spec Layer, start with the contribution guide.

pages.title: Quickstart: Figma docs and CLI setup | Spec Layer
pages.description: Create docs in Figma, copy context for AI, and connect a published library to your repository.
pages.content:
Docs
/
Quickstart
Get started with Spec Layer

Create docs in Figma, copy context into your coding agent, or publish a library for your repository.

Canvas documentation and Copy for AI are free. Publishing a library requires Pro. The CLI requires Node.js 22 or newer.
Document in Figma
Open Spec Layer

Install the plugin from Figma Community and run it in your design-system file.

Select your source

Select a component or component set to open its documentation options. For local variable collections and text styles, open Generate foundation docs in the sidebar.

Choose what to document

Choose the sections or sources you need and select Create docs. In the component screen, AI writing is optional: it assists the sections marked AI. Measurements, states, anatomy, and tokens come directly from Figma.

Review changes in the Library

Open Library and select Refresh library to check the sources. Review detected changes, then use Update documentation for one item or Update all docs for the changed docs.

Copy for AI

Copy for AI exports structured design context without making an AI request or consuming your writing allowance. You can copy directly from a selected component or a foundation source, without creating canvas docs first.

For a component, select Copy for AI in the footer. You get compact YAML with its properties, variants, states, anatomy, layout, and the token and style dependencies it uses. Paste that context into your coding agent with your implementation request.

button.ai.yaml · abbreviated synthetic example
Download full YAML 
component: { name: Button, related: [Icon] }
api:
  variants:
    Style: { options: [Filled, Outlined], default: Filled }
  states: [Enabled, Hovered, Disabled]
  booleans: { Show icon: { default: false } }
  slots: { Label: { type: text, default: Button } }

This is a synthetic Button example from the repository. The full file includes references, bindings, and the component’s foundation dependencies.

Copy a foundation source

In Generate foundation docs, use the copy button beside a variable collection or Text styles. This copies the selected source and its required local token dependencies as a compact Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) JSON document.

Foundation JSON preserves token types, values, modes, and references supported by the export. The document’s report records anything the DTCG format cannot express. Component context remains YAML.

A copy action does not change the sources selected for canvas docs. To keep context focused, copy the collection or component your agent needs.
Publish & pull

Publishing uploads the file’s foundation context and connected component contexts to Spec Layer. The CLI downloads that published bundle into your repository. It does not connect directly to Figma or generate UI code.

Publish from the plugin

Create docs for the components you want to include. Open Library, select Publish, then Publish library. When publishing finishes, select Copy setup command under Developer setup.

Connect your repository

Run the copied command from your project’s root directory. It already contains your library ID and pull key. The values below are placeholders.

npx spec-layer setup --id lib_... --key sl_...

Setup writes speclayer.json, stores the key in a gitignored speclayer.local.json, and pulls the artifacts into .speclayer/.

Refresh your local context

When the design changes, publish the library again from Figma. Then run the command below in your project to download the new version:

npx spec-layer pull
Copy
Updates are explicit: publish in Figma, then pull in your repository. status compares against the last published library. It cannot see unpublished changes in Figma.
Files added to your project
.speclayer/
├── bundle.json          # published library bundle
├── manifest.json        # artifact hashes and file paths
├── tokens/              # Foundation token files (CLI 0.4+)
└── ai/
    └── components/      # component YAML context

Point your coding agent at .speclayer/ai/ and .speclayer/tokens/. The bundle also retains the canonical artifacts when you need their full structure.

CLI versions: setup requires CLI 0.3.0 or later. Foundation output under tokens/ requires 0.4.0 or later. For automated workflows, install and pin the CLI as a development dependency.
Explore the CLI

Once setup is complete, use pull to download updates, status to check freshness, and list or show to inspect your local library.

Read the complete CLI command reference, including flags, selection rules, and exit codes.

Configure your project

Choose which components to pull, set the token value format, and keep your pull key separate from shared configuration. See configuration and pull keys.

Contribute

Spec Layer is MIT licensed. Read the contribution guide to set up the project or propose an improvement. Use synthetic or explicitly publishable fixtures.

pages.title: Output formats: component YAML and DTCG tokens | Spec Layer
pages.description: Canvas documentation, component YAML, foundation DTCG JSON, and the files written by Spec Layer.
pages.content:
Docs
/
Output formats
Understand the output

Choose canvas documentation for your team, compact exports for coding agents and token tools, or canonical JSON for validation and integrations.

Choose the right format
Output	Where to get it	Use it for
Canvas documentation	Create docs in Figma	Readable specs, measurements, anatomy, variants, and token references.
Component YAML	Copy for AI or ai/components/	Give a coding agent a component’s API, layout, and dependencies.
Foundation DTCG JSON	Copy a foundation source or read tokens/	Read token types, values, modes, and supported references.
Canonical JSON (full context)	show --canonical or the published bundle	Validate, inspect stable identities, and build integrations.

Extraction is deterministic. Previously saved AI-written guidance may accompany an export, but it is identified separately and excluded from semantic content hashes.

Component YAML

A component copy contains its properties, variants, states, anatomy, default-variant layout, and the token and style dependencies it uses. The dependency slice includes the local aliases needed to interpret those references.

Synthetic Button example · excerpt
Download full YAML
component: { name: Button, related: [Icon] }
api:
  variants:
    Style: { options: [Filled, Outlined], default: Filled }
  states: [Enabled, Hovered, Disabled]
  booleans: { Show icon: { default: false } }
  slots: { Label: { type: text, default: Button } }

The compact profile has spec_layer.version: 5 and profile: ai. Its hashes refer back to canonical context. It is not the canonical JSON shape and should not be validated against that schema.

Reference status makes missing information explicit: resolved, external, unavailable, not_in_snapshot, not_extracted, or no_foundation. Join references by resource kind and source ID, not by display name.

Foundation DTCG JSON

Foundation copies use a Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) resolver document. The CLI writes its file-based equivalent under tokens/, using the Design Tokens Format and Resolver Modules 2025.10.

Token files are organized by collection and mode. Typography and effect styles have dedicated files when present. resolver.json describes how to select the files for a mode.

Synthetic semantic color · excerpt
Download example
{
  "$type": "color",
  "$value": {
    "alpha": 1,
    "colorSpace": "srgb",
    "components": [1, 1, 1],
    "hex": "#ffffff"
  }
}

spec-layer.meta.json retains source details such as Figma IDs and code syntax. report.json explains information the projection cannot express. These files contain metadata, not tokens. Exclude them from patterns that select token files.

Inspect the synthetic resolver and its linked files. For compatibility formats or explicit unit choices, see token output options.

Files written by a pull
.speclayer/
├── bundle.json
├── manifest.json
├── tokens/
│   ├── <collection>.<mode>.json
│   ├── styles.typography.json
│   ├── styles.effects.json
│   ├── resolver.json
│   ├── spec-layer.meta.json
│   └── report.json
└── ai/
    └── components/
        └── <component-name>.yaml

This example shows the files a pull can create. Token and component files depend on the published library and your selection. Component filenames are slugged; collisions receive numeric suffixes.

bundle.json
The published bundle, retained in full even when you select only some artifacts for separate files.
manifest.json
Library and publication information, bundle hash, output selection, and an index of artifact names, content hashes, and paths. An unselected artifact has aiPath: null.
tokens/ and ai/components/
The files your token tooling and coding agent usually read. The foundation entry’s manifest path points to tokens/resolver.json.
How updates affect files

The CLI stages output in .speclayer.partial and swaps it into place. Keep your own source files outside this managed output directory.

An unchanged bundle, selection, and token configuration produces no new writes. Republishing changes export IDs and timestamps, so the bundle and manifest can change even if their semantic content hashes stay the same.

Component YAML, token files, and semantic hashes stay stable when the underlying design data does not change. An unrelated foundation change can change the whole-foundation hash without changing a component whose dependency slice is unchanged.

Next

pages.title: CLI command reference | Spec Layer
pages.description: Spec Layer CLI setup, init, pull, status, list, and show commands, with flags, examples, and exit codes.
pages.content:
Docs
/
CLI commands
CLI command reference

Connect a published library, pull updates, and inspect the context in your repository. This reference covers CLI 0.4.0.

Requirements and installation

Use Node.js 22 or newer and run commands from your project root. Publishing requires Pro; pulling a library requires its ID and pull key. For your first connection, follow the setup instructions before running pull.

After setup, pull the published library
Copy
npx spec-layer pull

For automated runs, pin the documented CLI version as a development dependency:

Install a specific version
Copy
npm install --save-dev --save-exact spec-layer@0.4.0

npx spec-layer then uses the installed local version. If you deliberately use an uninstalled package in automation, npx --yes spec-layer … suppresses npm’s installation prompt.

setup

Save the library ID, store the pull key locally, and perform the first pull. Copy the real command from Library → Publish → Copy setup command after publishing.

npx spec-layer setup --id lib_... --key sl_...

The values above are placeholders. Setup writes speclayer.json and speclayer.local.json. Inside a Git repository, it checks that the key file is ignored before writing the key.

Re-running setup replaces the stored key while preserving the output directory, selection, and token options unless you explicitly override them. If the first pull fails, the saved setup remains available; retry with pull.

init

Write configuration without storing a key or making a network request. Use this when your key comes from an environment variable.

npx spec-layer init --id lib_... --out .speclayer

init overwrites speclayer.json. Use setup to replace a key while preserving existing settings.

pull

Fetch the last published library and write selected artifacts to the output directory. The default is .speclayer/.

Download the published version
Copy
npx spec-layer pull

The output must be inside the current directory. An existing non-empty directory that Spec Layer did not create is refused. With the same bundle, selection, and token options, an up-to-date pull writes nothing.

Design changes must be published from Figma before a pull can see them.

status

Compare the local copy with the published library without writing files. Exit code 2 means the copy is behind or no local pull exists yet.

Check published freshness
Copy
npx spec-layer status

This checks the published bundle, not unpublished Figma changes. If you changed output selection or token settings, run pull to apply them.

list

List every artifact in the last local pull, including its output path or an indication that it was not written separately. No network request or key is needed.

Inspect available artifacts
Copy
npx spec-layer list
show

Print one artifact from the local bundle. Components default to compact YAML; foundations default to the DTCG JSON document. Add --canonical for canonical Context JSON.

npx spec-layer show component Button
npx spec-layer show foundation
npx spec-layer show component Button --canonical
npx spec-layer show foundation --canonical

Quote names with spaces. An unknown or ambiguous component name produces an error rather than choosing a component for you. The command reads the full local bundle, even when the artifact was not selected for a separate file.

Selection flags

setup, init, and pull accept these options. They replace the configured selection for that command; they are not merged with it.

npx spec-layer pull --only foundation
npx spec-layer pull --only components
npx spec-layer pull --component Button --component "Text field"
npx spec-layer pull --only components --component Button
--only foundation writes foundation token files and no component YAML.
--only components excludes the foundation token directory.
--component NAME is repeatable and includes the foundation unless combined with --only components.
--only foundation cannot be combined with --component.

Names match by slug: Button matches button, and Icon Button matches icon-button. A name that matches nothing fails before output is written. The complete published bundle is still retained in bundle.json.

Other options
Option	Applies to	Behavior
--id ID	setup, init, pull, status	Select the published library. Required for setup and init.
--key KEY	setup, pull, status	Supply a pull key. Environment and local-key fallbacks are described in Configuration.
--out DIR	All commands	Choose the managed output directory or the local output to inspect.
--api URL	setup, pull, status	Override the API origin, normally https://api.spec-layer.com.
--canonical	show	Print canonical Context JSON instead of the default projection.
Exit codes
Code	Meaning
0	Success. For status, the local copy matches the published library.
1	Usage, configuration, key, component-name, network, or server error.
2	Status only: local context is behind or no local pull exists.

Current commands are setup, init, pull, status, list, and show. There is no CLI validate, normalize, or diff command in this version.

pages.title: CLI configuration and design token options | Spec Layer
pages.description: Configure output selection, pull keys, token formats, unit overrides, and automated Spec Layer pulls.
pages.content:
Docs
/
Configuration
Configure your project

Keep shared project settings in speclayer.json and access keys outside version control. Configure which outputs your repository needs.

The project file

Run commands from the folder containing speclayer.json. Setup creates this file; you can then edit its output selection and token options.

speclayer.json · example
{
  "libraryId": "lib_...",
  "outDir": ".speclayer",
  "include": {
    "foundation": true,
    "components": ["Button", "Text field"]
  },
  "dtcg": {
    "values": "standard",
    "units": {
      "Foundation/spacing/*": "px"
    }
  }
}

Replace the library ID and component names with your own. The unit pattern is illustrative; it only applies when your collection and variable names match.

Field	Default	Purpose
libraryId	Set by setup	The library published from Figma.
outDir	.speclayer	A managed output folder inside your current directory.
include.foundation	true	Whether to write foundation token files.
include.components	All, when omitted	An array of component names. An empty array selects none.
dtcg.values	standard	The value representation used for token files.
dtcg.units	No overrides	Explicit unit assignments for otherwise unitless numbers.
Choose what to pull

Without an include block, a pull writes the foundation and all components. Save a list in the project file to make later pulls use the same selection.

Command-line selection flags override that selection for the command. They replace it entirely rather than adding to it. setup and init save an explicit selection; pull applies one for the current run.

npx spec-layer pull --component Button
npx spec-layer pull --only components --component Button

The first command includes the foundation; the second excludes it. Both retain the full published bundle in bundle.json. Selection controls separate output files, not access to individual records.

Pull keys

setup stores your key in speclayer.local.json. Inside a Git working tree, it confirms the file is ignored before writing the key. Shared configuration and generated outputs do not contain that key.

For pull and status, key precedence is:

--key
The SPEC_LAYER_KEY environment variable
The local key file, when it belongs to the selected library

Setup takes its key from --key or SPEC_LAYER_KEY. If a key changes, copy the new setup command from the plugin and run it again. Setup preserves existing output, selection, and token settings when no override is supplied.

To rotate a key, open Library → Publish and select Rotate key. Previous keys stop working within about a minute. Give the new setup command to every developer who needs access.

Token output options

dtcg.values accepts standard or legacy. Standard uses the 2025.10 object forms. Legacy uses string forms for integrations that expect them. Select the form supported by your token tooling.

dtcg.units maps a collection name plus a variable-name glob to px or rem. Use it to declare a unit for a number whose Figma scopes do not state one. Spec Layer does not infer a unit from the variable’s name.

"units": {
  "Foundation/spacing/*": "px",
  "Foundation/radius/*": "px"
}

An override that conflicts with an explicit source scope is ignored and reported in tokens/report.json. A changed dtcg block is applied by the next pull, even if nobody republished the library.

Use resolver.json to identify the token files for the mode you need. Exclude spec-layer.meta.json and report.json from patterns that select token files.

These options control the files generated by pull. show foundation prints the DTCG document stored in the bundle, rather than regenerating it with your local options.
Use in automation

Pin the CLI as a development dependency and provide SPEC_LAYER_KEY through your CI provider’s secret store. Keep speclayer.json alongside your project.

Run after dependencies and secrets are available
Copy
npx spec-layer status

Treat exit 0 as current, 2 as behind or not yet pulled, and 1 as an error requiring attention. Run pull when you want to update generated context. Do not treat every nonzero exit as stale data.

SPEC_LAYER_API overrides the default API origin for network commands; --api takes precedence. Keep the default unless you operate a different Spec Layer API.

Common setup issues
No local pull found
Run the setup command from the plugin or run pull from your configured project directory.
The key belongs to another library
Run the setup command for the library you want. A local key for a different library is not reused.
The key file is already tracked
Remove speclayer.local.json from Git tracking, keep it ignored, then run setup again. Rotate the key if it was shared.
The output directory is refused
Choose a new or empty folder inside your project, or use an existing Spec Layer output folder. Keep hand-written files elsewhere.

pages.title: Context JSON schemas and validation | Spec Layer
pages.description: Canonical Component and Foundation Context v5 schemas, versioning, required fields, and validation boundaries.
pages.content:
Docs
/
Schemas
Schemas and validation

The canonical schemas define the full Context v5 artifact. Use them when validating exports or building tools that consume Spec Layer data.

Download the schemas

Both schemas use JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 and describe schema version 5.1.0. These downloads are copies of the extractor’s committed schemas.

Component Context v5
Canonical JSON Schema · 5.1.0
Foundation Context v5
Canonical JSON Schema · 5.1.0

The schema identifiers are the component schema URI and the foundation schema URI. Their v5 paths identify the major contract; check spec_layer.schema_version for the exact artifact version.

Validate canonical JSON against these schemas. Component clipboard YAML, foundation DTCG JSON, and the outer library bundle are different shapes.
Get a canonical artifact

After pulling a library, add --canonical to show. Redirection below saves the JSON to a local file.

npx spec-layer show component Button --canonical > button.json
npx spec-layer show foundation --canonical > foundation.json

Use your component’s actual name. The canonical envelope includes spec_layer.kind, schema_version, schema_uri, extractor metadata, export metadata, and source identity.

The current Context version is 5.1.0. Component AI copies instead use the compact envelope version: 5 and profile: ai.

Component fields

The component schema describes one component and its scoped foundation dependencies. Fields below are listed from the downloadable schema.

Field	Required	Purpose
spec_layer	Yes	Schema, extractor, export, and source metadata.
foundation_content_hash	No	Identity of the complete source foundation.
foundation_dependency_hash	No	Identity of the component’s foundation dependency slice.
foundation_diagnostics	No	Foundation findings accompanying the component.
component	Yes	Component name and related components.
api	No	Component properties, variants, states, booleans, and slots.
anatomy	Yes	Named parts with exact path identities.
layout	No	Layout specifications for the default variant.
references	Yes	Used resources, bindings, and the scoped foundation context.
effects_inline	No	Effect properties attached directly to component nodes.
unbound	No	Hardcoded or unbound component values.
diagnostics	Yes	Reported extraction or validation findings.
validation	No	Derived component findings.
guidelines	No	Optional saved AI-written guidance, outside semantic hashes.

Bindings identify a resource by kind and source_id. Names are readable labels. A failed ID lookup is reported through reference status rather than resolved to an unrelated same-named resource.

Foundation fields

The foundation schema retains collection and mode identities, typed token values, alias information, and typography/effect styles. Fields below are listed from the downloadable schema.

Field	Required	Purpose
spec_layer	Yes	Schema, extractor, export, and source metadata.
completeness	Yes	What was readable and which sources were unavailable.
collections	Yes	Collection identities, modes, and source information.
tokens	Yes	Token identities, types, values, and aliases by mode.
styles	Yes	Typography and effect style definitions.
diagnostics	Yes	Reported extraction or validation findings.
statistics	Yes	Counts and extraction statistics.
guidelines	No	Optional saved AI-written guidance, outside semantic hashes.

Collections and styles can be partially available. Check completeness and diagnostics before assuming a file represents every source in the original Figma library.

Validate outside the plugin

Use a validator that supports Draft 2020-12, such as Ajv’s 2020-12 implementation. Save both schemas, a canonical button.json, and the example validation script in your project. The component schema references definitions in the foundation schema, so pass it as a dependency:

npm install --save-dev ajv
node validate-context.mjs component-context-v5.schema.json button.json foundation-context-v5.schema.json

To validate a foundation, pass its schema and canonical artifact:

node validate-context.mjs foundation-context-v5.schema.json foundation.json

The script loads the files you supply and does not fetch schemas from the network. It exits with 0 on success and 1 on a schema, data, or file error. This is a standalone validation example, not a Spec Layer CLI command.

What schema validation tells you

It checks structural requirements such as required fields and supported value shapes. It does not by itself establish that every Figma source was readable, all references resolve, or an interface is accessible.

Inspect diagnostics and reference status alongside schema validity. The extractor separates structural checks from referential integrity and completeness concerns.

Identity and content hashes

Use stable source IDs for identity. Names may change or collide. A component binding uses both resource kind and source ID; a token value is associated with a mode ID rather than only a mode name.

spec_layer.export.content_hash identifies semantic content. Export timestamps, export IDs, generated prose, and diagnostic wording do not define that identity. Component context also identifies the full source foundation and the dependency slice it uses.

Canvas drift hashes are separate from exported semantic hashes. Do not treat every metadata change as a design change or use a whole-foundation hash as a substitute for a component’s own content hash.

Library bundle version

The published bundle has its own envelope: schema: "spec-layer-library-bundle" and version 1.0.0. It contains foundation and component entries with their projections and canonical artifacts.

The ai field in a foundation entry contains the serialized DTCG JSON document; in a component entry it contains YAML. Despite the shared field name, the formats differ.

The current CLI reads bundle major version 1. The bundle parser checks the transport envelope; that is separate from validating each canonical Context artifact. See the bundle contract for the exact structure.

Support
Support

Last updated 6 September 2026

Spec Layer is maintained by an independent developer. Email oleksandr.kurchev@gmail.com and expect a reply within a few business days.

Before you write
License key not accepted. The plugin's License screen tells you whether the key is invalid, expired, disabled, or already active on the maximum number of devices. For the device limit, free a device in Manage subscription and try again. If the screen says verification is temporarily unavailable, your plan has not changed; try again in a minute.
AI writing did not run. The frame is still created; AI sections carry a placeholder. The License screen shows your remaining free uses. Failed calls do not count against them.
Publishing failed. The Publish screen names the reason: a Pro license is needed, the library is over the 5 MB limit, the license already publishes 10 libraries, or a source component could not be read. Nothing partial is published.
The pull key was rotated. Developers get a message from the CLI naming the fix: run the new setup command copied from the plugin's Publish screen.
Refunds. Within 30 days, for any reason. See the Refund Policy.
What to include
Which screen you were on and what you clicked.
The exact message the plugin showed, if any.
Your Lemon Squeezy order number for billing questions, never your license key.

Please do not send private design files. If a problem depends on a specific component, a description of its structure is enough to start with.

Security

To report a vulnerability, follow the responsible disclosure policy instead of this address.

Spec Layer
/
Privacy Policy
Privacy Policy

Last updated 6 September 2026

This policy explains what data the Spec Layer Figma plugin handles and why. Spec Layer is provided by Oleksandr Kurchev (the "Provider", "we", "us"), an individual acting as the data controller. You can reach us at oleksandr.kurchev@gmail.com.

Our starting point is to collect as little as possible. The plugin has no user accounts, and everything deterministic (measurements, states, anatomy, tokens) runs locally in Figma without sending your data anywhere.

What we collect
Libraries you publish. When you use Publish for developers (a Pro feature), the plugin uploads a bundle containing the component and token data from your connected documents: names, descriptions, variants, properties, token bindings, and resolved values, plus any AI-written text already on the canvas. Our proxy stores that bundle so the developers you share the pull key with can fetch it with the spec-layer CLI. The pull key itself is stored on our side only as a SHA-256 digest. The plain key is returned once, when the library is created; the plugin keeps it in Figma's client storage on your machine so its Publish screen can show the setup command again.
Component content you choose to document. When you use an AI-written documentation feature, a derived summary of the component you select (such as layer names, text, and structure) and, when it fits the size limits, a rendered image of that component are sent to our proxy and on to our AI provider. Foundation group writing sends the selected token names and resolved values, but no component image. This happens only when you ask for AI writing.
License, identity, and usage data. The free tier uses your Figma user identifier to maintain a quota; our backend stores it only as a salted SHA-256 digest. If you activate Pro, the plugin stores the license key in Figma's local plugin storage and our proxy sends it to Lemon Squeezy for validation. Our backend uses unsalted SHA-256 digests, not raw license keys, for cache keys, quota identities, and logs. We also process generation counts and timestamps to apply free-tier limits and Pro fair use. We do not build a profile of your designs.
Order information. When you buy Pro, Lemon Squeezy shares limited order details with us (such as your email and order identifier) so we can issue and manage your license key.

We do not collect payment card details. Those are handled entirely by Lemon Squeezy.

How we use it
to generate the documentation you ask for;
to validate your license and apply your plan's usage allowance;
to detect and prevent abuse and enforce fair use;
to provide support and process refunds.

Our legal bases are performance of our contract with you (providing the plugin and Pro features) and our legitimate interest in keeping the service secure and preventing abuse.

AI processing

AI-written documentation is generated by Anthropic using its Claude models. The content you submit is sent to Anthropic through our proxy solely to produce your documentation. Anthropic says commercial API inputs and outputs are not used for model training by default and are normally deleted from its backend within 30 days, subject to its stated legal, safety, and contractual exceptions. To avoid repeated processing, our proxy may cache a generated response for up to 24 hours under a content-derived key; it does not cache the submitted prompt or image.

Service providers (sub-processors)
Anthropic: AI generation of documentation.
Cloudflare: hosting of our proxy and license infrastructure.
Lemon Squeezy: payments and subscription management (merchant of record).
Figma: the environment the plugin runs in.

Each provider processes data under its own privacy terms. Some may process data outside your country; where that happens, appropriate safeguards apply.

Data retention

We keep license and usage records for as long as your subscription is active and for a reasonable period afterwards to meet legal and accounting obligations. For AI writing, our proxy does not persist submitted component summaries, rendered images, or token values. It may retain the generated response for up to 24 hours for idempotent retries. Anthropic's standard API retention is described in the AI processing section above.

A published library bundle is different: it is stored until you publish a newer version, which replaces it, and it is not deleted automatically when your subscription ends. There is no self-service unpublish yet. To have a library removed, email oleksandr.kurchev@gmail.com with the library id shown on the plugin's Publish screen.

Your rights

Under the GDPR and similar laws, you can request access to the personal data we hold about you, ask us to correct or delete it, object to or restrict certain processing, and request a copy in a portable format. To exercise any of these, email oleksandr.kurchev@gmail.com. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority.

Cookies

The plugin does not use advertising or tracking cookies. This marketing website does not set tracking cookies either.

Children

Spec Layer is a professional design tool and is not directed at children under 16.

Changes to this policy

We may update this policy from time to time. Material changes will be reflected by updating the date at the top of this page.

Contact

Questions about privacy? Email oleksandr.kurchev@gmail.com.

Terms of Service
Terms of Service

Last updated 6 September 2026

These terms govern your use of Spec Layer, a Figma plugin that turns components into specification and guideline frames. The plugin is provided by Oleksandr Kurchev (the "Provider", "we", "us"), an individual operating as a sole trader. You can reach us at oleksandr.kurchev@gmail.com.

By installing or using Spec Layer, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the plugin.

The service

Spec Layer reads the components, variables, and styles in your Figma file and generates documentation frames on your canvas, including measurements, states, anatomy, tokens, and optional AI-written usage notes. It can also copy the same design details to your clipboard as structured context for a coding agent, and, on the Pro plan, publish a library so developers can pull it into a repository with the spec-layer command-line tool. That tool is distributed on npm under the MIT license and is covered by these terms when it talks to our service. A free tier is available with no account and a limited AI allowance. A paid Pro subscription removes the fixed monthly AI cap for normal individual use and enables publishing, subject to the fair-use terms below.

Accounts and license keys

Pro is activated with a license key issued after purchase. You are responsible for keeping your license key confidential. A key is for your own use and may not be shared, resold, or used across multiple people or automated systems. We may limit or revoke a key that is used in breach of these terms.

Billing and merchant of record

Pro is sold as a subscription billed monthly or yearly. Payments are processed by Lemon Squeezy, which acts as the merchant of record for your purchase. Lemon Squeezy handles the transaction, invoicing, and applicable taxes, and your purchase is also subject to their terms. Subscriptions renew automatically until cancelled. You can manage or cancel your subscription at any time through the Lemon Squeezy customer portal.

Refunds

We offer a 30-day refund. See our Refund Policy for details on how to request one.

Fair use

Pro is intended for normal individual use. Documenting your library in a single sitting is fine. Automated, shared, or exceptionally high-volume usage may be limited under our fair-use policy. We will contact you before limiting anything.

AI-generated content

Some documentation is generated by a third-party AI model (see our Privacy Policy). AI output can be inaccurate or incomplete. You are responsible for reviewing generated content before relying on it. As between you and us, you own the documentation Spec Layer produces from your components, and you are responsible for ensuring you have the rights to the content you submit for processing.

Acceptable use

You agree not to:

use the plugin to break the law or infringe someone else's rights;
reverse engineer, resell, or redistribute the plugin except as allowed by law;
circumvent usage limits, license checks, or the billing system;
submit content you do not have the right to process.
Intellectual property

The Spec Layer plugin, its name, and its branding belong to the Provider. These terms do not transfer any ownership of the plugin to you. Your components and the documentation generated from them remain yours.

Third-party services

Spec Layer runs inside Figma and relies on third-party services including Figma, Lemon Squeezy (payments), Anthropic (AI generation), and Cloudflare (hosting of our proxy). We are not responsible for those services, and your use of them is subject to their own terms.

Disclaimer of warranties

The plugin is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind, to the fullest extent permitted by law. We do not guarantee that the plugin will be uninterrupted, error-free, or fit for a particular purpose.

Limitation of liability

To the fullest extent permitted by law, the Provider will not be liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from your use of the plugin. Our total liability for any claim relating to the plugin is limited to the amount you paid us in the twelve months before the claim. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited under applicable law, including your statutory consumer rights.

Termination

You may stop using the plugin at any time. We may suspend or end your access if you breach these terms. On termination, your right to use Pro features ends.

Changes to these terms

We may update these terms from time to time. Material changes will be reflected by updating the date at the top of this page. Continued use after a change means you accept the updated terms.

pages.content:
Spec Layer
/
Security & responsible disclosure
Security & responsible disclosure

Last updated 6 September 2026

We take the security of Spec Layer seriously. If you believe you have found a security vulnerability in the Spec Layer plugin or its backend, we want to hear from you and will work with you to resolve it.

Reporting a vulnerability

Email oleksandr.kurchev@gmail.com with the details. Please include:

a description of the issue and its potential impact;
clear steps to reproduce it, ideally with a proof of concept;
the affected component (the Figma plugin or the backend endpoint).

Please do not include real credentials or private design-system data in your report. Give us a reasonable amount of time to investigate and fix the issue before disclosing it publicly.

What to expect
We aim to acknowledge your report within a few business days.
We triage and fix confirmed issues ourselves and will keep you informed of progress.
We are happy to credit you once the issue is resolved, if you would like that.

Spec Layer is maintained by an independent developer. We do not currently run a paid bug-bounty program.

Scope

This policy covers the Spec Layer Figma plugin, the spec-layer command-line tool, the backend they talk to, and the library store that holds published bundles. The backend runs on Cloudflare Workers, a managed runtime that Cloudflare keeps patched, so there is no server or operating system for us to maintain. Our Anthropic API key is held server-side and never reaches the plugin. Prompts, rendered images, and generated text are never logged. The Worker receives a raw license key only to validate it with Lemon Squeezy; its own cache keys, quota identities, and logs use unsalted SHA-256 digests. Free-tier Figma identifiers use a separate salted SHA-256 digest. Payments are handled by Lemon Squeezy as merchant of record, so we never handle payment card data.

Safe harbor

If you make a good-faith effort to comply with this policy during your research, we will consider your testing to be authorized, and we will not pursue legal action against you. Please act in good faith: avoid privacy violations, data destruction, and any disruption of the service, and only interact with accounts or data that belong to you.

Contact

Security questions or reports: oleksandr.kurchev@gmail.com.

Refund Policy
Refund Policy

Last updated 22 July 2026

We want you to be happy with Spec Layer Pro. If it does not work out, we offer a straightforward refund.

30-day refund

You can request a full refund within 30 days of your purchase, for any reason. This applies to your initial purchase and to each renewal charge within its own 30-day window.

How to request a refund

Email oleksandr.kurchev@gmail.com from the address you used to buy, or include your Lemon Squeezy order number. We will confirm and process the refund. Payments and refunds are handled by Lemon Squeezy, our merchant of record, so the refunded amount is returned to your original payment method by Lemon Squeezy, typically within a few business days depending on your bank or card provider.

After a refund

When a refund is issued, the associated Pro license key is deactivated and Pro features stop working. You can keep using the free tier.

The free tier

Spec Layer has a free tier that needs no payment and no account, so you can try the core functionality before subscribing to Pro.

Your statutory rights

This policy is in addition to any refund or cancellation rights you have under applicable consumer law. Nothing here limits those rights.

Contact

Questions about a refund? Email oleksandr.kurchev@gmail.com.
